nodes.label: Fail-Closed Renderer
nodes.rationale: Every patch entry wraps in try/catch; on first exception the renderer disables for the session and logs once so a broken visual plugin never crashes or spams the render loop.

nodes.label: Game-to-Render Snapshot
nodes.rationale: The render patch must not touch game-world objects. Plugin.Update builds an immutable AuroraSnapshot on the game thread; the render thread reads the latest snapshot and camera-relative planet center.

nodes.label: Patch After Atmosphere
nodes.rationale: Harmony postfix on MyAtmosphereRenderer.RenderGBuffer is the first unconditional transparent-stage step, so aurora composites over atmosphere haze while clouds and billboards composite over the aurora. Clouds Render is gated by a debug override.

nodes.label: Aurora Borealis with Planet Screenshot
nodes.rationale: In-game night still from a planet surface looking over snowy peaks; no HUD. Green aurora fills the sky above terrain, framed as aurora with a planet rather than from space.

nodes.label: Additive Aurora Transparency
nodes.rationale: Stars and the galactic band remain visible through the green curtains, so the aurora composites additively over the skybox.

nodes.label: Aurora Spill on Terrain
nodes.rationale: Snow on the right-center peaks picks up a faint green tint under the bright curtain, emission reaching the planet surface.

nodes.label: Green-to-Teal Altitude Gradient
nodes.rationale: Right-hand band is bright emerald; left-hand curtains fade through teal into the deep-blue horizon.

nodes.label: Vertical Curtain Rays
nodes.rationale: Left-side drapery shows distinct vertical columns from zenith toward the peaks, curtain morphology rather than a flat glow sprite.

nodes.label: Aurora From Orbit Screenshot
nodes.rationale: In-game still from space looking down on a snowy planet limb; no HUD. Green aurora curtains wrap the curved horizon against a starry, cloudy sky.

nodes.label: Additive Aurora Transparency
nodes.rationale: Stars remain visible through the green curtains, so the aurora composites additively over space rather than as an opaque sheet.

nodes.label: Green-to-Teal-to-Blue Gradient
nodes.rationale: Peak brightness is emerald on the left curtains and fades through teal into deep blue on the right limb, matching altitude/view-angle falloff.

nodes.label: Limb-Following Aurora Band
nodes.rationale: The green band traces the planet's curved horizon rather than sitting as a sky dome, showing the effect is altitude-bound to the limb from orbit.

nodes.label: Vertical Curtain Rays
nodes.rationale: Bright columns remain visible along the left limb, the same curtain morphology as ground views, not a flat glow sprite.

nodes.label: Aurora Night Landscape Screenshot
nodes.rationale: HUD-less in-game still from a snowy ridge looking slightly up. The sky, not the terrain, is the subject: a green aurora band in a starry night with broken clouds.

nodes.label: Additive Aurora Transparency
nodes.rationale: Point stars remain visible through the green curtains, so the aurora is composited additively over the sky instead of as an opaque sheet.

nodes.label: Clouds Occlude Aurora
nodes.rationale: Dark broken clouds sit in front of parts of the green band; glow shows only in gaps. The aurora is a sky effect behind weather, not a post overlay on the whole frame.

nodes.label: Emerald Green Emission
nodes.rationale: Peak color is saturated emerald in the mid-sky; edges fall off to teal and then the dark blue of the night sky. No red or purple band is visible.

nodes.label: Sky-Only Aurora Composite
nodes.rationale: Snow and rock stay in unlit night values; the aurora does not light the terrain. The effect is confined to the sky behind the ridge silhouette.

nodes.label: Vertical Curtain Rays
nodes.rationale: The green band is built from many vertical columns that drop toward the horizon, the curtain morphology of a real aurora rather than a single sprite or horizontal wash.

nodes.label: Anomaly Owns Shared Rendering Gaps
nodes.rationale: When this pack invents lighting, IsolatedMix energy, or march LOD that the next Anomaly shader will also need, file it on Anomaly Docs/Extensibility.md Slice AI and wiki/Framework-gaps.md rather than leaving it pack-private.

nodes.label: Rich HUD Config Save Rule
nodes.rationale: Rich HUD sliders must not serialize or write config on every tick; ControlChanged fires continuously and per-tick XmlSerializer I/O can queue GPU work until a later device hang.

nodes.label: Azimuthal Noise UV
nodes.rationale: Longitude/latitude noise UVs smeared into radial spokes at the pole; sampling on the azimuthal tangent-plane projection also removes the ±π seam.

nodes.label: Bounded Fixed-Step March
nodes.rationale: Quality presets use a fixed 24/48/96 step loop instead of the Unity while loop so GPU cost is bounded.

nodes.label: Fullscreen Pass for v1
nodes.rationale: MyScreenPass.DrawFullscreenQuad plus a custom pixel shader is enough for v1 because the ray/shell miss early-outs in a few ALU ops; a proxy mesh is a later optimization.

nodes.label: Use Game Shader Registry
nodes.rationale: MyPixelShaders.Create registers ps_5_0 __pixel_shader bytecode so live reload and device-reset recompile come for free, unlike raw D3DCompiler.

nodes.label: March Both Shell Segments
nodes.rationale: Marching only the first shell segment left a hard edge along the inner sphere tangent when the camera was inside the shell; both segments are marched as one continuous arc length.

nodes.label: Skip Unity Depth Reconstruction
nodes.rationale: Unity repo scene-depth reconstruction is dead code never used; SE uses its own depth occlusion against resolved scene depth.

nodes.label: Spherical Shell Instead of Box
nodes.rationale: Unity marches an axis-aligned box in a flat sky; SE planets are spherical, so the volume is a spherical shell segment between inner and outer radii, masked to a polar latitude band.

nodes.label: Aurora Over Mountains Screenshot
nodes.rationale: In-game night still looking up from snow-capped peaks; no HUD. Central subject is a green aurora band in a starry, cloudy sky.

nodes.label: Additive Aurora Transparency
nodes.rationale: Stars remain visible through the green curtains, so the aurora composites additively over the sky rather than as an opaque sheet.

nodes.label: Green-to-Teal Altitude Gradient
nodes.rationale: Peak brightness is emerald in the lower-middle band and fades to teal then deep blue toward the zenith.

nodes.label: Vertical Curtain Rays
nodes.rationale: Bright columns run zenith-to-horizon across the green band, the classic curtain morphology rather than a flat glow sprite.
